lessons.title: 1.1 Semantic Landmarks & Accessible Structure
lessons.summary: Why header, nav, main, article, and section tags matter for screen readers and SEO.
lessons.content:
Semantic HTML communicates meaning rather than mere presentation. Screen readers rely on landmark elements such as <header>, <nav>, <main>, <aside>, and <footer> to jump directly between regions of a page.

Key Principles:
1. Use exactly one <h1> per view representing the primary topic, followed sequentially by <h2> and <h3>.
2. Pair every form <input> with an explicit <label for="..."> element.
3. Use <button> for actions and <a href="..."> for navigation—never attach click handlers to plain <div> tags.

lessons.title: 1.2 Mastering CSS Grid & Flexbox Alignment
lessons.summary: Choosing between 1D Flexbox tracks and 2D CSS Grid templates.
lessons.content:
Modern CSS separates one-dimensional distribution (Flexbox) from two-dimensional page architecture (CSS Grid).

- Flexbox excels at navigation bars, button toolbars, and aligning items along a single main axis with justify-content and align-items.
- CSS Grid lets you define explicit columns and rows simultaneously using grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)).

Tip: Combine gap utilities instead of fragile negative margins to keep spacing consistent across breakpoints.

lessons.title: 2.1 Asynchronous JavaScript & Fetch Lifecycle
lessons.summary: Understanding Promises, async/await, HTTP status codes, and error boundaries.
lessons.content:
Web applications communicate with backend servers over HTTP using asynchronous requests.

When calling fetch(url):
1. Always check response.ok (HTTP 200–299) because fetch only rejects on network failure, not HTTP 404 or 500 responses.
2. Parse JSON via await response.json().
3. Wrap requests in try/catch blocks and surface actionable error feedback to the user.

lessons.title: 2.2 Event Delegation & Client State Hygiene
lessons.summary: Preventing memory leaks and securing user-generated output against XSS.
lessons.content: Whenever displaying user-entered text in the DOM, prefer textContent over innerHTML to avoid Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). On the server, always validate request payloads independently of client-side form checks.

lessons.title: 1.1 Python Built-in Collections: List, Tuple, Set, Dict
lessons.summary: Comparing mutability, ordering, and lookup performance across Python collections.
lessons.content:
Choosing the right collection directly impacts both clarity and runtime speed:

- list: Ordered, mutable sequence. O(1) append, O(n) membership check.
- tuple: Ordered, immutable sequence. Ideal for fixed records and dictionary keys.
- set: Unordered unique elements backed by a hash table. O(1) average membership check.
- dict: Key-value mapping preserving insertion order (Python 3.7+). O(1) average lookup.

lessons.title: 1.2 Writing Clean Functions & List Comprehensions
lessons.summary: Default arguments, pure functions, and readable comprehensions.
lessons.content: Avoid mutable default arguments such as def add_item(item, target=[]): because the default list is shared across every call. Instead, use target=None and initialize inside the function body.

lessons.title: 2.1 Time Complexity & Binary Search
lessons.summary: Why sorted arrays unlock O(log n) search performance.
lessons.content: Linear scan checks elements one by one in O(n) time. Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval, finding a target among 1,000,000 items in at most 20 comparisons—O(log n).

lessons.title: 1.1 Primary Keys, Foreign Keys & Normalization (1NF–3NF)
lessons.summary: Eliminating update anomalies through clean relational table decomposition.
lessons.content:
Relational databases prevent data duplication and inconsistency through normalization:

- 1NF: Every column holds atomic values; no repeating groups.
- 2NF: Every non-key attribute depends on the entire primary key (no partial dependencies).
- 3NF: No transitive dependencies between non-key attributes.

Foreign keys enforce referential integrity so child rows cannot reference non-existent parent records.

lessons.title: 2.1 SQL JOINs, Aggregations & ACID Transactions
lessons.summary: Combining tables accurately and wrapping multi-step writes in transactions.
lessons.content:
An INNER JOIN returns only rows matching in both tables, whereas a LEFT JOIN preserves all rows from the left table even when no right-hand match exists.

When submitting an examination or transferring funds, wrap all INSERT and UPDATE statements in a database transaction (BEGIN; ... COMMIT; or ROLLBACK;) so partial failures never corrupt state.

lessons.title: 1.1 Propositional Logic & De Morgan Laws
lessons.summary: Logical equivalence, implications, and negating compound statements.
lessons.content:
De Morgan Laws state that:
- NOT (P AND Q) is logically equivalent to (NOT P) OR (NOT Q)
- NOT (P OR Q) is logically equivalent to (NOT P) AND (NOT Q)

Understanding implication (P -> Q) is equally crucial: it is false only when P is true and Q is false.

lessons.title: 1.1 Sentence Clarity, Parallelism & Concise Argumentation
lessons.summary: Structuring topic sentences and eliminating wordy passive constructions.
lessons.content: Effective technical and academic writing places the primary subject and active verb early in the sentence. Parallel structure ensures items in a list or comparison share the same grammatical form.

lessons.title: 1.1 How DNS, HTTP & TLS Protect Web Traffic
lessons.summary: From domain lookup to encrypted transport over HTTPS.
lessons.content: When you enter a web address, DNS resolves the human-readable hostname into an IP address. TLS then establishes an encrypted tunnel using asymmetric handshake keys before HTTP requests travel across the network.

questions.prompt: Which HTML5 element should wrap the primary unique content of a document for accessibility landmarks?
questions.explanation: The <main> landmark identifies the dominant content of the <body> and allows assistive technologies to skip repeated navigation.

questions.prompt: When using the JavaScript fetch() API, how does it handle an HTTP 404 Not Found response?

options.text: It automatically throws a TypeError exception
It resolves the Promise with response.ok set to false
It retries the request three times before rejecting
It returns null instead of a Response object

questions.explanation: fetch() only rejects on network failures or aborted requests; HTTP error statuses like 404 or 500 resolve with response.ok === false.

questions.prompt: Which CSS layout model is specifically designed for simultaneous two-dimensional (row and column) alignment?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid controls rows and columns simultaneously, whereas Flexbox is designed for single-axis (1D) layout.

questions.prompt: Explain the security difference between inserting user-supplied text with element.textContent versus element.innerHTML, and describe how to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in a web form.
What is the average-case time complexity of checking membership (x in collection) in a Python set?
questions.explanation: Python sets are implemented using hash tables, enabling O(1) average-case membership lookup.

questions.prompt: Which Python data type is immutable and hashable (when containing hashable elements), making it valid as a dictionary key?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable sequences and can serve as dictionary keys if all of their elements are also hashable.

questions.prompt: Why is using a mutable default argument like def append_score(s, items=[]): discouraged in Python?

options.text: Python raises a SyntaxError on empty lists in function signatures
The default list is created once at function definition and shared across calls
Lists inside function parameters are automatically converted to tuples
It slows down garbage collection by 10x

questions.explanation: Default parameter expressions are evaluated once when def executes, causing mutations to persist across subsequent calls.

questions.prompt: Describe how binary search works on a sorted Python list and explain why its worst-case time complexity is O(log n) rather than O(n).
Which SQL JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table, filling unmatched right columns with NULL?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table regardless of whether a matching record exists in the right table.

questions.prompt: In relational database normalization, what does Third Normal Form (3NF) specifically eliminate?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires a table to be in 2NF and have no non-key column depend transitively on the primary key via another non-key column.

questions.prompt: In ACID database transactions, what does the "A" (Atomicity) property guarantee?

options.text: All statements inside a transaction succeed together or roll back completely
Queries run asynchronously without locking rows
Tables are automatically backed up every hour

questions.explanation: Atomicity ensures an all-or-nothing unit of work: either every operation commits or all changes are rolled back.

questions.prompt: Explain why saving a student examination submission (inserting student answers and computing the final result row) should be wrapped inside a database transaction.
According to De Morgan’s Laws, the negation of (P AND Q) is logically equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Negating a conjunction distributes the negation and flips AND to OR: !(P && Q) === (!P || !Q).

questions.prompt: How many distinct 3-letter subsets can be chosen from a set of 5 distinct letters {A, B, C, D, E}?
Under what condition is the logical implication P → Q evaluated as FALSE?

options.text: When P is false and Q is false
When P is false and Q is true
When P is true and Q is false
When both P and Q are true

questions.explanation: An implication P → Q is only false when the hypothesis P holds true yet the conclusion Q fails.

questions.prompt: Which sentence demonstrates correct parallel grammatical structure?

options.text: The platform helps students to read lessons, taking quizzes, and track scores.
The platform helps students read lessons, complete quizzes, and track scores.
The platform helps students reading lessons, to complete quizzes, and tracking scores.
The platform helps students read lessons, completing quizzes, and score tracking.

questions.explanation: All three verb phrases ("read lessons", "complete quizzes", "track scores") share the consistent base verb form.

questions.prompt: Choose the most concise active-voice revision of: "The final examination results were published by the academic committee."

options.text: The academic committee published the final examination results.
Publication of the final examination results was done by the committee.
By the academic committee, the final examination results got published.
There was a publication of final examination results by the committee.

questions.explanation: Active voice puts the actor ("The academic committee") first followed directly by the strong verb ("published").

questions.prompt: Which network protocol is responsible for translating human-readable domain names (like edutrack.edu) into IP addresses?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) maps domain names to numerical IP addresses.

questions.prompt: Why should server-side applications hash passwords using an algorithm like scrypt or bcrypt rather than storing plain text or reversible encryption?

options.text: Hashing allows administrators to email forgotten passwords back to users
One-way salted hashing prevents attackers from recovering original passwords if a database leaks
Hashing reduces the database file size by 90%
Browsers require hashed passwords to render login forms

questions.explanation: Salted, slow one-way hashing ensures passwords cannot be reversed or cracked easily with precomputed rainbow tables.

studentAnswers.writtenText: Binary search starts by checking the middle index of a sorted list. If the target value is smaller, we discard the upper half; if larger, we discard the lower half. Because each step cuts the remaining search space by 50%, the maximum number of comparisons grows logarithmically as O(log n).
